title: The Bulge, the Sauer and Sibret, 16 December 1944 - 3 January 1945
eyebrow: The 60th Armored Infantry Battalion's after action reports

participants.name: 9th Armored Division
participants.note: its Combat Command A fought both actions, the 60th Armored Infantry Battalion in it

paras.text: On the morning of 16 December 1944 the German attack in the Ardennes reaches the 9th Armored Division's quiet sector on the Sauer, held by the 60th Armored Infantry Battalion; for five days the battalion and Combat Command A hold the southern shoulder between Beaufort and Ermsdorf. On the 26th the command is sent west, and from the 27th to 3 January it fights beside the corridor just opened to Bastogne, at Sibret and Chenogne. Told here from the battalion's own after action reports for December and January, as a transcription gives them, beside the German side as the Army's official history tells it; no German record is read yet.

On the Sauer the battalion's three rifle companies were cut off on the second day: by darkness on 17 December the Germans were in Beaufort, contact with the companies was lost, and at 1743 the headquarters withdrew to Savelborn [[cite:eucmh60aib/1944-12]]. Their remnants came back through the German lines on the nights of 18-20 December, and from the 19th the battalion held a line from Waldbillig to Ermsdorf, where it beat off attacks on the 21st and 23rd [[cite:eucmh60aib/1944-12]]. Cole names what it faced as the 276th Volks Grenadier Division, whose commander was killed during the attack, and puts the division's furthest advance at Waldbillig on the 20th [[cite:cole/9/p232]] [[cite:cole/9/p236]].

Sent to the Bastogne corridor, Task Force Collins (the battalion, with tanks, tank destroyers and engineers attached) took Sibret on 27 December, attacked toward Chenogne, and was driven back to the high ground north of Sibret by a German counterattack that the battalion estimated at a brigade; it attacked again on 1 January, and was relieved by the 17th Airborne Division on the 3rd [[cite:eucmh60aib/1944-12]] [[cite:eucmh60aib/1945-01]]. For the month of December the report counts 1 officer and 63 men killed, 4 and 156 wounded and 4 and 141 missing [[cite:eucmh60aib/1944-12]].

The two accounts don't agree on the days at Chenogne. The battalion's report has it attacking the town on the 30th and the German attack coming at 0530 on the 31st; Cole has its tanks in the village late on the 29th and the Fuehrer Begleit Brigade's attack beginning at 0730 on the 30th [[cite:cole/24/p616]] [[cite:cole/24/p619]]. Which is right needs the original report or a German record (Questions and sources).

The transcription types no zone letters ("at 1743"). The times are taken as A (UTC+1), the letter the Army's reports in this theatre type (III Corps' "1550A" at Remagen [[cite:iiicorps-aar-1945-03/p72]]), as the 12th Army Group's maps' hour is: assumed, not typed. Cole's times are the US records' where he gives them; his one German time, the 3d Panzer Grenadier Division's planned 0730 on the 30th, is German time, which in winter was also UTC+1. Most entries carry only a day.

Under the entries, the front and the divisions are the 12th Army Group's situation maps for 1200 on each day from 16 December to 3 January, traced [[cite:loc-12ag/ict21195]]: the army group's own units and its intelligence picture of the Germans', each symbol in its unit's area, not at a position (`fronts/README.md`). The symbols are read on every sheet of the window. They are divisions and above: the 9th Armored is one "9(-)" that the army group moves between its parts (by Beaufort on the 18th, by Bastogne on 20-22 December, by Étalle and Paliseul from the 23rd), and Combat Command A, at Sibret and Chenogne from the 27th, has no symbol of its own; the sheets can also run days behind a move (`fronts/README.md`). The towns are drawn at their centres (OpenStreetMap): the reports name villages, not grid references, except the command post's "9136" on the 19th, which names no sheet and is not placed. The 60th's dashed line is its own stations, joined straight, to the day shown. The relief is today's; the Sauer and the Our, too small for the river data used, show only as their valleys.

The battalion's reports are read in a transcription by the European Center of Military History, on a page that is now gone (read through the Internet Archive); it has no page numbers and has not been checked against the original in the National Archives (RG 407). It has at least one slip, "Dec 19" for the 27th. The German side is Hugh Cole's official history, *The Ardennes* (1965), which drew on the German commanders' postwar manuscripts: it is secondary here until those, or the war diaries of the 276th Volks Grenadier Division, LXXX Corps, the 26th Volks Grenadier Division and the Fuehrer Begleit Brigade, are read.

Still to read: the 9th Armored Division's and Combat Command A's after action reports for December; the 19th Tank Battalion's and the 89th Cavalry Reconnaissance Squadron's; the battalion's original report; and the German records.

events.placed: The month's totals, as the report gives them
events.words: Personnel losses, each line as typed: "Killed – 1 Off & 63 EM", "Died of wounds – O Off & 1 EM", "Wounded or injured – 4 Off & 156 EM", "Missing – 4 Off & 141 EM", "Captured – 0 Off & 2 EM". And: "During the month the following damages and casualties were inflicted on the enemy : Killed : 578; Prisoners : 518; Wounded : 327; AT Guns 3 (88-MM); Vehicles : 4."
events.note: The enemy's losses are the battalion's own count, not a German record

events.words: "By Dec 10, at 1110, the battalion completed relieving the 2/109, in a sector of the line assigned to 9-AD. From Dec 10 to Dec 15, the 60-AIB occupied and defended the assigned sector. We patrolled actively along our front but nothing took place to change this sectors reputation of being exceptionally quiet."
events.note: The report names no village for the sector; Beaufort is where its company command posts were on the 17th, and Cole has the battalion's headquarters there (p. 231)

events.words: "The center German regiment, 988th, made its crossings near Dillingen, aiming in the direction of Beaufort and Haller. Here Company A was deployed in the woods above the Sauer ... By noon the attack threatened to overrun the company and infiltration had taken place at several points".

"The situation became increasingly critical due to our over extended front and, by noon, Baker Company, the reserve company, less its AT Plat was committed between Able and Charlie Cos with the mission of driving through and clearing the enemy from the near bank of the Our and the Sauer Rivers. After meeting heavy opposition, Baker Co finally succeeded in occupying a position abreast of Able and Charlie Cos."

events.actor: The German attack (as the 60th's report gives it)
events.words: "On Dec 16, 0630, the Germans attacked our sector following over a 1000 rounds artillery preparation consisting chiefly of Nebelwerfer and medium caliber artillery. The attacking force was estimated at two infantry regiments, one to attack the battalion and the other to move through and attack positions to our rear. ... The two main routes of infiltration were through the draws at Dilligen and Grundhof. ... Vehicular bridges were established across the Sauer River at Dillegen, Wallendorf and Grundhof."
events.note: The US side's account of the attack; the town is spelled Dilligen and Dillegen in the transcription

events.placed: Cole's "before 0630", the time the first boats landed; no German time is given
events.words: "In any case there was considerable confusion and delay on the east bank, and few or none of the rubber assault boats landed on the American side before 0630. ... The main crossing was made by the 986th Regiment near Wallendorf."
events.note: Cole (p. 229) has the 276th (Generalleutnant Kurt Moehring), just in from Poland, "generally" facing the 60th Armored Infantry Battalion, between Wallendorf and Bollendorf; its artillery and train horse-drawn, no assault guns

events.placed: Cole types no time ("during the morning")
events.words: "On the south the 987th Regiment, thus far missing in American identifications of the 276th Volks Grenadier Division, appeared during the morning. One of its battalions marched unopposed through the Schwarz Erntz gorge and occupied Müllerthal".

"After continued request for reinforcements, the morning of Dec 17, CCA/9-AD, having taken command of this sector at 1100, attached Troop A, 89th Cavalry Reconnaissance Squadron to the battalion, and the 3-FAB assigned 3 medium tanks."

"By late afternoon the situation again became more critical and by darkness snipers had worked into Beaufort. All contact was lost with the front line companies and could not be restored. The 81-MM mortar platoon was ambushed attempting to move into position and all company OP's in Beaufort were attacked and forced to withdraw with all Company Commanders cut off from their companies. With the enemy in control of Beaufort and enemy patrols attempting to cut the only withdrawal route, Beaufort – Haller road, at 1743, the Hq & Hq Co (minus) withdrew to the Battalion Motor Park in the vicinity of Savelborn."

events.placed: Cole's time for the cavalry's rear guard (from the US records); the attack began "at dark"
events.words: "The chief German success on 17 December came at the close of day, with an attack by the 1st Battalion, 988th Regiment, on Beaufort. ... at dark Germans seeped into the town from assembly points in the woods ... The cavalry unit, led by Capt. Victor C. Leiker, held on until 2030, by which time the German infantry controlled all the street corners, then fought its way south to Waldbillig."

events.actor: A battalion of the 986th Regiment, with an antitank company
events.words: "The American setback had stemmed from the last act of General Moehring as commander of the 276th. Moehring had collected a battalion of the 986th Regiment and an antitank company armed with fifty-four Panzerfausts for an attack across the Savelborn-Ermsdorf road to seize Medernach. ... There it lay, with perfect cover for close-in work with the bazooka, when the American advance began."
events.note: In the Eselbour woods. Cole (p. 234): "The Americans lost seven tanks before the order finally came to withdraw." Moehring was killed in his staff car between Beaufort and Müllerthal (p. 232); Cole gives no date, and has Colonel Hugo Dempwolff take over the division (p. 235)

events.words: "The attack proceeded as planned but encountered heavy enemy opposition at the Line of Departure ... At 1600, Dec 18, after an advance of 1500 yard the task forces were withdrawn. An enemy force of approximately 70 men engaged the Command Post in a fire fight from 0730 to 1400, personnel, drivers and small administrative groups from Co CP's threw back all attempts to take over the place and at 1400, 50 prisoners of the afore mentioned group surrendered. Throughout the day 250 enemy prisoners were taken and about 100 others were killed."
events.note: CCA's counterattack toward Beaufort was set for 0300; the report gives 1600 for its withdrawal

events.placed: "On the morning of Dec 19"; no time typed
events.words: "During the night of Dec 18/19 the remnants of Able Co and the MG platoon successfully withdrew from their Beaufort position and were placed in the defensive line. On the morning of Dec 19, the defensive line Waldbillig – Ermsdorf was strengthened ... The 60-AIB's CP was moved to 9136."
events.note: The four-figure reference 9136 names no map sheet, so the CP is not placed; the line is drawn at Waldbillig

events.words: "During the night of Dec 19/20 the remnants of Baker and Charlie Cos arrived in an area near Fels, Luxembourg. This withdrawal was executed just prior to an enemy attack by troops estimated the size of Battalion preceded by an artillery preparation to wipe out the surrounded companies."

events.placed: "In midafternoon" for the attack, "when night fell" for the village; Cole types no time
events.words: "In midafternoon on 20 December the weapons remaining to the company, apparently not more than three or four, joined the 988th at Haller and the attack against Waldbillig commenced. ... when night fell Dempwolff brought the 987th Regiment through Müllerthal and into the gorge running west to Waldbillig. ... The capture of Waldbillig on 20 December marked the high-water mark of the 276th Volks Grenadier Division advance."
events.note: The 60th's report doesn't mention Waldbillig after the 19th

events.words: "From Dec 20 to Dec 23, our line was strengthened and Charlie Co was moved up to occupy the right portion of our sector. On Dec 21, an attack by about 60 enemy infantrymen on Charlie Co's right flank was quickly repulsed."

"On Dec 23, an enemy counterattack was launched by two infantry companies and two S/P 75-MM guns on the right of the sector at Savelborn. The entire attack was repulsed with heavy losses. On Dec 24, Baker Co was attached to 19t-TB. From Dec 23 to Dec 26, the activity on both sides was limited to a heavy exchange of artillery fire and probing patrols."
"At 1600, Dec 26, the 60-AIB was relieved in the Savelborn sector and as part of CCA, 9-AD, moved immediately to Longlier, Belgium."

"Arriving at 2345, CCA, was attached to the 4th Armored Division and orders were issued for an attack at 0800, on Dec 19, along the Neufchateau – Bastogne road to take the high ground southwest of Bastogne and make contact with friendly units in the town."
events.note: "Dec 19" as transcribed; the attack was the next morning, 27 December (the report's own next sentences, and Cole p. 615)

events.placed: Day only; the attack was ordered for 0800
events.words: "The 60-AIB and attachments were organized as Task Force Collins (Lt Col Kenneth W. Collins) ... The first resistance encountered was in vicinity of Sibret, Belgium. 40 PW's being taken. A PW stated they were left behind to cover the withdrawal of the main body to Saint-Hubert, Belgium. Light resistance was also encountered in capturing the towns of Jodenville and Flohamont. ... At darkness road blocks were established surrounding Sibret. Charlie Co patrolled the town throughout the night and Able Co occupied the high ground north of Sibret."
events.note: Task Force Collins was the battalion less Baker Co, with Charlie Co of the 19th Tank Bn, a platoon of the 9th Armored Engineers, the 811th Tank Destroyer Bn and a section of the 482nd AAA AW Bn

events.placed: Cole types no time ("It took all night")
events.actor: A detachment of the 104th Panzer Grenadier Regiment
events.words: "Collins sent his single company of Shermans into Sibret, firing at everything in sight. The Americans could not be said to hold the village, however, for a small detachment of the 104th Panzer Grenadier Regiment was determined to make a fight of it and did. It took all night to drive the German grenadiers out of the cellars and ruined houses."
events.note: Cole (p. 615): the sector was General Kokott's, his 26th Volks Grenadier Division and its attached battalions of the 15th Panzer Grenadier Division

events.words: "On Dec 28, Able Co, with Charlie 19-TB attached, attacked the woods to north of the former position but were driven back by heavy enemy fire. Throughout the remainder of the 28 as well as the 29, vigorous patrolling was carried out. Enemy activity was relatively inactive."

events.placed: "While at breakfast"; Cole types no time
events.actor: A company of the 26th Volks Grenadier Division's pioneers
events.words: "In the meantime General Kokott had gathered a counterattack force, a company of the division Pioneers, to retake Sibret. While at breakfast on the 29th ... Collins' troops suddenly saw a body of men march out of the nearby woods. ... The Americans cut loose with every weapon, to such effect that some fifty dead Germans were counted".
events.note: The 60th's report has the 29th as patrolling, "Enemy activity was relatively inactive"

events.placed: "Late in the day"; Cole types no time
events.words: "Late in the day, however, the fortunes of war turned against the Americans. Collins' tanks had moved through the village square in Chenogne and were approaching a road junction when high velocity shells knocked out the two lead tanks. Then, in a sharp exchange of shots, the enemy gunners accounted for two more of the Shermans, and the Americans withdrew."
events.note: Cole (p. 616): Remer's brigade "already had taken some share in the action against CCA", one of its 105-mm. flak pieces holding up Task Force Collins at the roadside woods. The 60th's report has Chenogne taken on the 30th (Questions, below)

events.words: "On Dec 30, Task Force Collins attacked and took Chenogne. Charlie Co lead in the attack and after stiff fighting cleared all enemy resistance from high ground south of Chenogne and heavy woods to the right. Able Co supported by Charlie 19-TB then passed through and cleared the town of Chenogne. At darkness our troops pulled back and occupied the high ground south of the town and an attached Recon platoon of Troop B, 89th Reconnaissance Squadron out posted the town."

events.placed: "As dusk came"; Cole types no time
events.words: "As dusk came Remer set about pulling his command together, and the 3d Panzer Grenadier --heeding his call for assistance--moved troops into the ruins of Chenogne."

events.placed: The time Cole gives for the German plan ("planned to attack at 0730"), which he says Remer kept
events.actor: Fuehrer Begleit Brigade, with the 3d Panzer Grenadier Division
events.words: "Generalmajor Walter Denkert, commanding the 3d Panzer Grenadier Division, planned to attack at 0730 on 30 December ... Remer also kept to his time schedule. The Fuehrer Begleit advance was geared for a one-two punch at Sibret. ... The grenadier battalion made some progress and drove Task Force Collins back toward Sibret, but the battalion commander was killed and the advance slowed down."
events.note: Pages 619-620. The 60th's report has the attack south from Chenogne at 0530 on the 31st (Questions, below)

events.actor: The enemy (as the 60th's report gives it)
events.words: "At 2000, the enemy attacked with an unknown number of tanks and infantry and drove our out post from Chenogne to our position south of the town. At 2400, the enemy probed our lines with two tanks and a platoon of infantry along the Sibret – Chenogne road but were repulsed."

events.actor: The enemy (as the 60th's report gives it)
events.words: "On Dec 31, at 0530, the enemy launched a strong attack south from Chenogne apparently with the aim of cutting the Neuchateau – Bastogne road. This attack was launched by an enemy force estimated the size of a brigade. Of this, an estimated battalion of infantry and a company of tanks attacked our position both frontally and from the flanks. Able Co 60-AIB and Charlie Co 19-TB were forced from the high ground south of Chenogne ... The force of the attack struck the reserve position and was repulsed with very heavy losses."
events.note: The report names no German unit; Cole puts the Fuehrer Begleit Brigade's attack on the 30th

events.words: "Simultaneously with the enemy counterattack a Combat Command from the 11-AD was launching an attack northeast throughout Jodenville and this threat to his flank apparently caused the enemy to withdraw his forces to the high ground south of Chenogne. By noon our troops had been reorganized and the line firmly established."

"orders were received by Task Force Collins to attack that morning with the mission of clearing the heavy woods to the front and right front, and seize and occupy the high ground south of the railroad between Chenogne and Senonchamps. ... the attack which was set for 1100. ... Within some five or six hours after the attack began, the woods had been flushed, and Task Force Collins was digging in on its objective. ... In these woods we captured our first prisoners other than German (Polish, Czech, etc)."

"On the morning of January 2, these two troops attacked and cleared a small woods just north of the railroad finding therein only a few enemy stragglers. ... Later, Task Force Karsteter took the town of Senonchamps and the 11-AD made contact with elements of the 101-A/B north and east of Senonchamps."

"TF Collins remained in position until units of CCA were relieved the following afternoon, January 3, by elements of the 17-A/B. Upon relief of CCA, both Task Forces were disbanded and all attached elements reverted to their parent units."

claims.question: When did the German attack on the Sauer begin?
When did the German attack on the Sauer begin?
claims.note: Cole adds "considerable confusion and delay on the east bank"; he gives no German time for the crossing

claims.question: What attacked the 60th on the Sauer?
claims.answer: "Two infantry regiments", by the battalion's estimate
claims.note: "one to attack the battalion and the other to move through and attack positions to our rear"

claims.question: What attacked the 60th on the Sauer?
claims.answer: The 276th Volks Grenadier Division, its 986th and 988th Regiments, with the 987th on the south flank
claims.note: Pages 229-231. Cole: the 987th was "thus far missing in American identifications of the 276th" on the 17th. A German record (the division's or LXXX Corps' war diary) would settle it; none has been read

claims.question: What did the fight on the Sauer cost the 60th?
claims.answer: 1 officer and 63 men killed, 4 and 156 wounded, 4 and 141 missing, in the whole month
claims.note: The month's totals, Sibret and Chenogne included; the report doesn't split them by fight

claims.question: What did the fight on the Sauer cost the 60th?
claims.answer: "An estimated 231 casualties" in the three days
claims.note: Cole has volunteers leading back "nearly 60 percent of the armored infantry" from behind the German lines

claims.question: When was the attack from Longlier toward Sibret?
claims.note: The report arrives at Longlier at 2345 on the 26th and has Sibret taken by nightfall on the 27th, so the 19th is a slip, the transcriber's or the original's; the original hasn't been checked

claims.question: When was the attack from Longlier toward Sibret?
claims.note: Task Force Collins was "held up some hours by mines" north of Vaux-lez-Rosières

claims.question: When did Task Force Collins first get into Chenogne?
claims.answer: 30 December ("attacked and took Chenogne"), pulling back south of it at darkness
claims.note: The report has the 28th's attack on the woods driven back, and the 29th as patrolling

claims.question: When did Task Force Collins first get into Chenogne?
claims.answer: 29 December, late in the day, its tanks through the village square before four were knocked out
claims.note: Cole's "on the 8th" for the day before is a misprint for the 28th in this transcription (p. 616)

claims.question: When did the German attack south from Chenogne toward Sibret come?
claims.note: An enemy force "estimated the size of a brigade"; the battalion names no unit

claims.question: When did the German attack south from Chenogne toward Sibret come?
claims.answer: 30 December, from 0730, the Fuehrer Begleit Brigade with the 3d Panzer Grenadier Division
claims.note: Pages 619-620: Denkert's plan for 0730, which Remer kept; the grenadier battalion "drove Task Force Collins back toward Sibret". The two accounts are a day and two hours apart. The battalion's report for the 30th has its own attack on Chenogne and a German attack at 2000; a German record, or the original of the battalion's report, would settle which day

claims.question: What attacked from Chenogne?
claims.answer: "An enemy force estimated the size of a brigade", an infantry battalion and a tank company against the battalion

claims.question: What attacked from Chenogne?
claims.answer: The Fuehrer Begleit Brigade (Remer), attached to the 3d Panzer Grenadier Division
claims.note: Cole names the brigade's "about forty Mark IV tanks plus an assault gun brigade of thirty tubes" (p. 614)
